newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up 3.33 pct on rebound, finmin.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up 3.33 pct on rebound, finmin.

text.p: Thai stocks closed 3.33 percent higher on Friday on a technical rebound and expected appointment of banker Thanong Bidaya as new finance minister, brokers said.
The SET Index, closing at its new 98-month low on Thursday, gained 15.48 points to close at 480.25 on 5.04 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 1.57 points to 33.47.

"Investors, including foreigners, bought on expectation that Thanong could run the finance ministry although he is less popular than his predecessor Amnuay Viravan," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
Thanong, president of Thai Military Bank Plc, would succeed Amnuay who resigned from his job on Thursday.
Brokers said technical rebound was another major factor for the Friday rally as foreigners bought large capitalised bank, communications and energy issues.
All key sectors advanced on Friday.
Banks led the advance, rising 3.49 percent, the communications sector gained 6.27 percent, and the finance counter surged 3.75 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, gaining two baht to 75, Advanced Info rose nine to 143, and Siam Cement advanced 10 to 376.
Brokers said they expected the market to move sideways on Monday due to absence of fresh news.
